problem_text:
A retail distribution center must devise a procurement and stock management strategy for a critical product line over a business week of 7 days.  
The starting stock level at the opening of the planning interval is 7 units.  
In each day \( t = 1, \dots, 7 \), the vendor permits the center to submit a purchase request whose volume must fall within a range of 5 to 61 units.  
Nevertheless, every purchase request that is submitted will require 1 day(s) for delivery before it becomes available to meet customer requirements or to rebuild stock.  
The projected customer requirement for the product on each day is provided as follows:  

* Day 1: requirement 41 units  
* Day 2: requirement 26 units  
* Day 3: requirement 29 units  
* Day 4: requirement 59 units  
* Day 5: requirement 36 units  
* Day 6: requirement 34 units  
* Day 7: requirement 34 units  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will not be carried forward to later days.  
Throughout the planning interval, product volumes may be treated as continuous quantities, and the aggregate quantity of physical stock on the premises at any moment must not surpass the storage limit of 31 units.  

On the first day, the maximum purchase volume is restricted to 35 units.  
On the fourth day, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 9 units.  

The aggregate expenditure over the planning interval comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 2 per unit purchased; the storage expense, which amounts to 2 per unit of stock retained from one day to the next; and the stock‑out penalty, which amounts to 11 per unit of unfulfilled requirement.  
Please ascertain the optimal purchase volume for each day and monitor the consequent stock and shortfall levels in order to minimize the total expenditure.
